approved: The bill seeks approval for $13 billion in appropriations, including $5 billion for NBN Co., $3 billion for Defence equipment and facilities, and $2.4 billion for infrastructure projects such as Western Sydney Airport, Inland Rail, and WestConnex stage 2.

The Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2018-2019 was moved for a second reading, seeking just under $250 million for four parliamentary departments, including $193 million for the Department of Parliamentary Services with $2.9 million allocated to establish a Cyber Security Operations Centre for Australian Parliament House.
The speaker announced that unless otherwise ordered, five appropriation bills would be referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration at the adjournment of the House.

The budget delivers tax relief for over 75,000 people in Brisbane, a record $75 billion national infrastructure pipeline with over $20 billion for Queensland projects including the Brisbane Metro, and $1.3 billion for a National Health and Medical Industry Growth Plan, while contrasting Labor’s commitment to retaining a 49 per cent top marginal tax rate.

The speaker argued that the coalition government has delivered smaller government and greater equality of opportunity, citing over 21 community grants secured for Mackellar, including $10,000 for The Burdekin Association's youth hub, funding for the Davidson Rural Fire Brigade station upgrade, new computer equipment for the Tibetan Community in Australia, and a new vehicle for Easylink.

The speaker announced total appropriations of just under $108.5 billion for the 2018-19 financial year and just under $8 billion in supplementary appropriations, including $6.5 billion for the Department of the Environment and Energy—$6 billion for purchasing New South Wales and Victorian government shares in Snowy Hydro Limited and under $435 million for the Reef 2050 Long Term Sustainability Plan.
